newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian railways considering claim on Eurotunnel.
newsitem.headline: Belgian railways considering claim on Eurotunnel.

text.p: Belgium's National Railways (NMBS/SNCB) said on Monday it was considering suing Eurotunnel SA /Plc for damages following the closure of the tunnel under the British Channel.

The Channel Tunnel has been closed for a week following a fire, disrupting both the Shuttle rail service for vehicles and the Eurostar passenger service which connects London and Paris and London and Brussels.
"We are investigating what is possible, together with our partners and individually," NMBS director Leo Pardon told Belgian VTM television.
The partners in the Eurostar venture are British Rail and SNCF, the French railway operator.
The closure of the tunnel has led to a drain of passengers and traffic away to cross-channel ferry companies.

A NMBS spokesman later told BRTN radio, "It is the case we are suffering an important loss because we invested so much to build up Eurostar. In the last few months traffic and the number of passengers rose strongly and we hoped that in the Christmas and New Year period we would achieve a large increase."
Neither Pardon nor the spokesman gave an exact amount of the actual or likely losses.
"Due to the interruption of Eurostar for a number of days we think we will suffer quite a commercial loss, in addition to the fact that we cannot use our very expensive trains," the spokesman said.
He expected Eurotunnel to be insured for such events.
The SNCB would file any claim with the SNCF and British Rail since they had signed the contract for use of the tunnel with Eurotunnel. SNCB had no direct contract with Eurotunnel itself.
In Paris the SNCF also said it was looking at the possibility of claiming lost revenues from Eurotunnel. It said the amounts lost ran into several million francs per day.
The SNCF deplored a decision last Thursday by the Franco-British safety commission to allow only freight service through the tunnel.

Eurotunnel is insured for operating losses with French insurer UAP. A spokesman said it was too early to put figures to any Eurotunnel claim as the company and UAP were still evaluating the damage from last week's fire.
